subject: Astramed on‑prem integration sprint kickoff — network & storage alignment
messages:
From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay.rao@astramed.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lina Park <lina.park@astramed.com>
Date: 2027-05-23T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Kickoff — on‑prem integration sprint (network + storage)

Hi Stephanie,

Thanks for agreeing to run a short integration sprint with our infra team next week. We want to make sure the network and storage designs will meet our compliance needs (PHI segmentation, egress controls) before we schedule the on‑site run.

High level asks from our side:
- Confirm VLAN/IP plan and BGP peering options for the VPC interconnect
- Understand persistent volume binding model and expected IOPS for model serving
- Review KMS/HSM integration for key rotation during backups

Attached is our initial network diagram and a rough storage-sizing workbook — these are rough and will need your inputs. Can we do a 60‑minute working session on Tuesday 2027‑05‑25 10:00 PT? RackCorp (our datacenter provider) will join for crossconnect details.

Regards,
Sanjay Rao
VP Infrastructure, Astramed

Sanjay — thanks, that works. Tuesday 05/25 10:00 PT is good for us. Agenda proposal:

1) Quick introductions (10m)
2) Network topology and peering constraints (20m) — Karthik + RackCorp
3) PV model and performance expectations (15m) — Marissa
4) Security controls (KMS/HSM, audit logs, egress) (10m) — Neha
5) Action items & owners (5m)

Prep for our side: we'll bring a Redwood on‑prem checklist and a recommended PVC class mapping for model serving vs. logs/backups. Karthik — can you confirm we can produce a baseline IO profile for a 2048‑token request workload by Monday?

Stephanie
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sanjay Rao <sanjay.rao@astramed.com>, Lina Park <lina.park@astramed.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-24T14:16:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Kickoff — on‑prem integration sprint (network + storage)

Quick update — I pulled a 24‑hour token profile from a comparable healthcare workload and produced a conservative IOPS/throughput estimate. Short summary:
- Serving nodes (GPU): expected sustained read IOPS per pod ~ 250; burst up to 1200 for concurrent small requests; recommend NVMe cached PV for model weights and a separate PVC on blockstore for KV/cache persistency
- Logs & metrics: low IOPS, high throughput; recommend HDD-backed blockstore with daily archiving to S3 compatible object store via on‑prem gateway
- Snapshot cadence: hourly for KV cache, daily for model artifact backups (encrypted at rest)

I'll attach the rough table I used and can present the numbers Tuesday. Also note: if Astramed wants single‑AZ failover, we should size an extra hot spare GPU node pool.

Karthik
Senior Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Lina Park <lina.park@astramed.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sanjay Rao <sanjay.rao@astramed.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, RackCorp Ops <ops@rackcorp.net>
Date: 2027-05-25T08:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Kickoff — on‑prem integration sprint (network + storage)

Thanks team. A couple of clarifications ahead of the session:
- PHI segmentation: our security team requires that model inference traffic never traverse the same VLAN as general office traffic and all egress to cloud object store must be via a customer‑controlled NAT with firewall rules.
- KMS/HSM: we plan to use our on‑prem HSM for master key; Redwood will need to support external key wrap during snapshot creation
- RackCorp: can you confirm crossconnect MTU constraints and whether they support PTP for time sync (NTP/PTP)

We expect a 90‑minute working session if needed; please flag if Redwood needs more time.

Lina
SRE Lead, Astramed

From: RackCorp Ops <ops@rackcorp.net>
To: Lina Park <lina.park@astramed.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Kickoff — on‑prem integration sprint (network + storage)

On Tue, May 25, 2027 at 09:14 AM Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Agenda proposal:
> 1) Quick introductions (10m)
> 2) Network topology and peering constraints (20m) — Karthik + RackCorp
>
RackCorp here — crossconnect MTU is 9000 by default; we can negotiate jumbo frames down to 1500 if Astramed's edge gear requires it. We support BGP adjacency with MD5 and can provision a private VLAN trunk for PHI traffic; PTP is available on request but there may be a short provisioning lead (~48 hours) depending on the cage setup.

I'll have the crossconnect runbook and contact for the provisioning engineer in the working session.

— Ops Support, RackCorp

From: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>

Subject: Post‑meeting notes & required compliance artifacts

Thanks everyone for the productive session. Consolidated items and owners: 

1) Network separation: RackCorp to provision private VLAN (PHI) by 2027‑05‑27 — owner: RackCorp Ops
2) BGP & MTU: Karthik to validate BGP MD5 config template and test session in staging — owner: Karthik (due 2027‑06‑02)
3) PV mapping: Marissa to publish PVC class matrix (nvme-cache, block-ssd, block-hdd) + recommended ioLimits — owner: Marissa (due 2027‑05‑28)
4) KMS/HSM integration: Neha to produce key‑wrap integration doc and acceptance criteria for snapshot encryption (requires Astramed HSM cert) — owner: Neha (due 2027‑06‑04)
5) Audit logs: Stephanie to share Redwood log retention options and sample ELT pipeline for archived events — owner: Stephanie (due 2027‑05‑30)

Attachments: redwood-onprem-checklist-v2.docx, astramed-network-diagram-v1.pdf, storage-capacity-estimate-asm.xlsx

Next meeting: 2027‑06‑02 09:00 PT — BGP test & PV matrix review. Please reply if any owner needs more time.

Neha Kapoor
Security & Compliance Engineer, Redwood Inference
